questions.stem: Which pair of reusable modules forms the capstone's main workload foundation?

options.A: sql-managed-instance and Cosmos DB
options.B: Traffic Manager and Front Door
options.C: An external registrar and Public DNS only
options.D: network-core and windows-iis-vmss

optionExplanations.A: Those data modules are not used here.
optionExplanations.B: Neither global-routing service is deployed by this capstone.
optionExplanations.C: Public DNS is not the workload foundation.
optionExplanations.D: The configuration composes network and Windows IIS VMSS modules.

questions.stem: Which sequence matches the capstone's intended public web path?

options.A: Client to Key Vault to Log Analytics
options.B: Client to Standard Load Balancer to IIS VMSS
options.C: Client to Terraform state to SQL
options.D: Client to Bastion to a WAF

optionExplanations.A: Secret and log services are not HTTP relays.
optionExplanations.B: The VMSS module owns the Load Balancer web frontend and backends.
optionExplanations.C: No SQL path is deployed here.
optionExplanations.D: Bastion is for administration, not web delivery.

questions.stem: Which source is explicitly allowed for web-subnet RDP in the capstone?

options.A: Any Internet address
options.B: The GitHub Pages hostname
options.C: AzureBastionSubnet's 10.40.20.0/26
options.D: All addresses through a rule at priority 120

optionExplanations.A: The subsequent rule denies other RDP sources.
optionExplanations.B: A site hostname is not the configured source CIDR.
optionExplanations.C: The allow rule scopes RDP to the Bastion subnet.
optionExplanations.D: Priority 120 is the deny-other-RDP rule.

questions.stem: Internet RDP reaches the web NSG. Which explicit rule addresses sources not covered by the Bastion allow?

options.A: DenyOtherRdp at priority 120
options.B: AllowHttpFromInternet at priority 100
options.C: An automatic quiz-completion rule
options.D: The Key Vault /32 rule

optionExplanations.A: The higher-numbered RDP deny follows the specific allow.
optionExplanations.B: The HTTP rule applies to port 80.
optionExplanations.C: Progress does not configure an NSG.
optionExplanations.D: Vault rules protect a different service.

questions.stem: Why include Azure Bastion in this capstone?

options.A: Provide the private administration path to Windows instances
options.B: Terminate public HTTP for the Load Balancer
options.C: Store Terraform state snapshots
options.D: Create SQL database users

optionExplanations.A: Bastion provides managed RDP connectivity to private targets.
optionExplanations.B: The Load Balancer handles the web frontend.
optionExplanations.C: Backend state storage is a different service.
optionExplanations.D: No SQL database is created here.

questions.stem: Which dedicated subnet is declared for the Bastion host?

options.A: data-snet at 10.40.3.0/24
options.B: The GitHub runner subnet
options.C: AzureBastionSubnet at 10.40.20.0/26
options.D: The VMSS's public Internet subnet

optionExplanations.A: That workload subnet is not the Bastion resource's target.
optionExplanations.B: The runner is not an Azure subnet managed here.
optionExplanations.C: The exact Bastion subnet name and /26 are declared.
optionExplanations.D: VMSS instances use the private web subnet.

questions.stem: Which statement fits the public IPs in this capstone?

options.A: Each VMSS instance is assigned its own public IP here
options.B: Load Balancer and Bastion have public frontends while VMSS instance NICs use private addresses
options.C: The Key Vault has a dedicated VM public IP resource
options.D: The workspace routes every HTTP request

optionExplanations.A: The module's instance NIC configuration is private.
optionExplanations.B: Public frontend resources do not require per-instance public NIC addresses.
optionExplanations.C: No such vault VM IP resource is declared.
optionExplanations.D: A workspace is not a web proxy.

questions.stem: What resource declares outbound behavior for the VMSS backend pool?

options.A: A Traffic Manager priority
options.B: An inbound RDP allow only
options.C: A Private DNS registrar record
options.D: A Load Balancer outbound rule

optionExplanations.A: DNS routing does not provide outbound SNAT.
optionExplanations.B: Inbound administration does not define egress.
optionExplanations.C: Private DNS is not an outbound translation service.
optionExplanations.D: The module explicitly defines web-outbound.

questions.stem: Why does the module's HTTP Load Balancer rule set disable_outbound_snat=true?

options.A: It disables all VMSS Internet access permanently
options.B: It prevents inbound port 80 traffic
options.C: Outbound SNAT is separately defined by the outbound rule
options.D: It enables SQL private access

optionExplanations.A: An outbound rule is also configured.
optionExplanations.B: The setting does not remove the inbound HTTP rule.
optionExplanations.C: The explicit outbound rule controls egress for that pool.
optionExplanations.D: SQL is not part of this capstone.

questions.stem: The probe resource is named http-probe. Which protocol does its configuration actually use?

options.A: TCP on port 80
options.B: HTTPS with path /health
options.C: HTTP with path /admin
options.D: RDP on port 3389

optionExplanations.A: The code explicitly sets protocol Tcp and port 80.
optionExplanations.B: No HTTPS monitor path is configured.
optionExplanations.C: No HTTP path is configured in this probe.
optionExplanations.D: RDP is not the web-health probe.

questions.stem: The TCP port-80 probe is healthy. Which additional evidence should still be collected?

options.A: Every application transaction is guaranteed correct
options.B: The VMSS password was rotated automatically
options.C: All Log Analytics tables contain data
options.D: A real HTTP request returns the expected service response

optionExplanations.A: A probe cannot prove every transaction.
optionExplanations.B: Probe health does not rotate credentials.
optionExplanations.C: Probe health does not configure log collection.
optionExplanations.D: A TCP listener does not prove complete application behavior.

questions.stem: How does the VMSS module configure the demonstration IIS page?

options.A: Key Vault renders the page
options.B: A Custom Script Extension installs Web-Server and writes index.html
options.C: Bastion writes every HTTP response
options.D: The NSG compiles an IIS module

optionExplanations.A: Key Vault stores secrets.
optionExplanations.B: The extension runs the Windows bootstrap commands.
optionExplanations.C: Bastion is an administration service.
optionExplanations.D: NSGs filter network traffic.

questions.stem: Apply completes but the first HTTP request fails. What should be inspected?

options.A: Only the site's dark theme
options.B: Extension progress, probe health, NSG, and backend membership
options.C: Only workspace retention
options.D: Only the random suffix length

optionExplanations.A: Docs theme cannot affect IIS.
optionExplanations.B: Provisioning can precede a healthy application path.
optionExplanations.C: Retention is unrelated to HTTP reachability.
optionExplanations.D: Name length does not prove application readiness.

questions.stem: Bastion cannot reach a VMSS instance. Which set follows the lesson's troubleshooting?

options.A: Traffic Manager targets and DNS TTL only
options.B: SQL admin login and blob subresource only
options.C: Quiz score and progress import only
options.D: Bastion subnet, RDP NSG source, instance health, and credentials

optionExplanations.A: No Traffic Manager path is deployed here.
optionExplanations.B: Those services are not the RDP target.
optionExplanations.C: Browser progress is not connectivity evidence.
optionExplanations.D: The administration path has network, host, and identity requirements.

questions.stem: Key Vault returns Forbidden to the applying workstation. What should be checked?

options.A: Current public /32, applying identity policy, and propagation
options.B: Whether public HTTP port 80 is open
options.C: Whether the Load Balancer probe is named http
options.D: Whether the book's PDF downloaded

optionExplanations.A: The vault has its own network and authorization boundary.
optionExplanations.B: HTTP NSG admission does not grant vault access.
optionExplanations.C: A probe name does not authorize secret reads.
optionExplanations.D: Book downloads are unrelated.

questions.stem: What does the generated Windows password supply in this capstone?

options.A: Only a public README example
options.B: SQL Managed Instance login
options.C: VMSS administrator input and a Key Vault secret
options.D: The browser progress export password

optionExplanations.A: The value is not published in README.
optionExplanations.B: No SQL Managed Instance is deployed.
optionExplanations.C: The same generated credential is passed to the VMSS and stored in the vault.
optionExplanations.D: Progress is not password protected by this credential.

questions.stem: Which production improvement is still needed beyond the capstone's password wiring?

options.A: Assume VMSS already fetches the secret using managed identity
options.B: Share the generated password in public outputs
options.C: Replace TLS with plain text everywhere
options.D: Managed identity secret retrieval and coordinated rotation

optionExplanations.A: No managed identity retrieval flow is declared.
optionExplanations.B: Publishing the credential expands exposure.
optionExplanations.C: Weakening transport security is not the stated improvement.
optionExplanations.D: The current module receives the generated password directly.

questions.stem: The password is in Key Vault. What Terraform artifact still needs sensitive handling?

options.A: Only the SVG diagram
options.B: Only resource-group tags
options.C: State and potentially saved plans
options.D: Only module source folder names

optionExplanations.A: The illustration contains no generated password.
optionExplanations.B: Tags are metadata.
optionExplanations.C: Generating and assigning credentials stores values in Terraform artifacts.
optionExplanations.D: Folder names are not credential values.

questions.stem: What does creating Log Analytics alone establish in this capstone?

options.A: Automatic collection of every VM log
options.B: A workspace boundary, not guaranteed VM telemetry collection
options.C: A configured alert for every failure
options.D: Automatic incident response

optionExplanations.A: A workspace does not automatically attach all agents and sources.
optionExplanations.B: Collection and alert configuration require additional production work.
optionExplanations.C: No universal alert setup is declared.
optionExplanations.D: Incident handling needs its own design.

questions.stem: Why keep instance_count small during the capstone?

options.A: Each instance adds VM and disk costs
options.B: It changes the PDF license
options.C: It reduces the required NSG rule name length
options.D: It eliminates Bastion's fixed hourly cost

optionExplanations.A: Scale count multiplies compute and disk capacity.
optionExplanations.B: Compute sizing does not change licensing notices.
optionExplanations.C: Rule names do not set compute cost.
optionExplanations.D: Bastion cost is independently incurred.

questions.stem: Which prerequisite specifically guards against an expensive failed capstone attempt?

options.A: A matching browser color scheme
options.B: A 100 percent quiz score as cloud permission
options.C: Quota and budget for Bastion and the intended VMSS size/count
options.D: A public registrar transfer

optionExplanations.A: Theme does not reserve quota or budget.
optionExplanations.B: Quiz scores do not authorize Azure deployments.
optionExplanations.C: The deployment combines high-cost compute and administration services.
optionExplanations.D: This capstone does not require domain transfer.

questions.stem: Does the VMSS module automatically create autoscale rules in this capstone?

options.A: Yes; every VMSS implicitly scales by CPU
options.B: No; instance_count is configured and autoscale is a production addition
options.C: Yes; Key Vault controls scale count
options.D: Only if the workbook is downloaded

optionExplanations.A: VMSS capability alone does not create a policy.
optionExplanations.B: The capstone does not declare an autoscale setting.
optionExplanations.C: Vault storage does not scale compute.
optionExplanations.D: Book access has no compute effect.

questions.stem: The module declares upgrade_mode=Manual. What should a production plan include?

options.A: A deliberate rollout and patching strategy for instances
options.B: Assume every instance automatically adopts all future model changes
options.C: Disable backups to save update time
options.D: Use DNS TTL as the patch schedule

optionExplanations.A: Manual mode needs an intentional operational update approach.
optionExplanations.B: Automatic rollout is not implied by Manual.
optionExplanations.C: Recovery remains important.
optionExplanations.D: DNS caching is unrelated to VM updates.

questions.stem: The demo Load Balancer URL uses HTTP. What should a production gap review include?

options.A: Assume Standard Load Balancer terminates HTTPS certificates
options.B: Use the Key Vault secret name as a TLS certificate
options.C: Treat TCP port 80 as encrypted traffic
options.D: TLS and appropriate application-layer protection

optionExplanations.A: A network Load Balancer does not provide managed TLS termination.
optionExplanations.B: A password secret name is not a certificate.
optionExplanations.C: HTTP on port 80 is not inherently encrypted.
optionExplanations.D: Production needs an intentional TLS/application gateway or Front Door design.

questions.stem: Why pass subnet_id and explicit VM inputs into the VMSS module?

options.A: Keep reusable component dependencies and configuration explicit
options.B: Let the module discover arbitrary tenant networks
options.C: Hide every resource from Terraform state
options.D: Make every caller share one global name

optionExplanations.A: Clear inputs make module composition reviewable.
optionExplanations.B: Uncontrolled discovery would blur ownership and scope.
optionExplanations.C: Module resources remain managed in state.
optionExplanations.D: Caller prefixes and context still determine resource names.

questions.stem: Why split platform, network, security, and workloads into reviewed states/modules for production?

options.A: Guarantee no dependencies remain
options.B: Allow every destroy to delete the whole tenant
options.C: Eliminate the need for identity scoping
options.D: Reduce lifecycle coupling and assign clear ownership

optionExplanations.A: Dependencies still require contracts and coordination.
optionExplanations.B: Broad destruction is contrary to scoped ownership.
optionExplanations.C: Least-privilege identities remain required.
optionExplanations.D: Separate lifecycles reduce unintended shared-resource deletion risks.

questions.stem: Which set best supports this capstone's acceptance criteria?

options.A: Only Terraform's final Apply complete line
options.B: Only the illustrated architecture
options.C: HTTP 200, NSG rule inspection, Bastion/vault state, and outbound-rule readback
options.D: Only a browser score of 100 percent

optionExplanations.A: Apply success alone is narrower than acceptance evidence.
optionExplanations.B: A diagram is not live validation.
optionExplanations.C: The set checks actual resource and application outcomes.
optionExplanations.D: A score is learner progress, not Azure evidence.

questions.stem: The production gap exercise should rank items using which considerations?

options.A: Only how colorful their icons are
options.B: Security risk, availability impact, operational effort, and cost
options.C: Only alphabetical service order
options.D: Only the number of Markdown lines

optionExplanations.A: Artwork does not rank production risk.
optionExplanations.B: The exercise asks for a prioritized engineering gap list.
optionExplanations.C: Alphabetical order does not prioritize impact.
optionExplanations.D: Line count does not measure operational importance.

questions.stem: After capstone destroy, which evidence matches the documented expected outcome?

options.A: Only the VMSS is stopped
options.B: Only the Load Balancer page times out
options.C: Managed state is empty and the lesson resource group no longer exists
options.D: Only the browser status says Complete

optionExplanations.A: Stopped resources can remain billable.
optionExplanations.B: An outage does not prove every resource was removed.
optionExplanations.C: State plus Azure readback checks the managed lifecycle removal.
optionExplanations.D: Local status is self-reported.

questions.stem: The active capstone group is gone. What should secret cleanup evidence still acknowledge?

options.A: All historic passwords are guaranteed securely erased
options.B: A deleted group grants anonymous access to retained secrets
options.C: The VMSS keeps serving through the deleted Load Balancer
options.D: Key Vault may be soft-deleted and local artifacts may retain credentials

optionExplanations.A: Destroy does not promise secure erasure of all history.
optionExplanations.B: Deletion does not authorize anonymous retrieval.
optionExplanations.C: Deleted owned networking cannot provide that original service path.
optionExplanations.D: Service retention and artifact handling are separate from active deletion.
